title: The edge-on galaxy NGC 1055
caption: The edge-on galaxy NGC 1055, imaged by the Very Large Telescope

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This colourful image from ESO's Very Large Telescope shows NGC 1055, a large galaxy in the constellation of Cetus, the Sea Monster. It is thought to be up to 15 percent wider than our own Milky Way.

NGC 1055 is classed as a spiral galaxy, yet it seems to lack the sweeping arms that spirals are known for. That is simply a matter of angle. We see it edge-on, so its disc appears as a narrow band and the arms are hidden from view, much as the pattern on a plate disappears when you look at it from the side.

The edge-on view does reveal something odd, since the galaxy's structure shows strange twists rather than lying perfectly flat. These twists probably came from an interaction with a large neighbouring galaxy. The FORS2 instrument took the data, using several filters, one of which isolates the glow of hydrogen gas.
scale: NGC 1055 is thought to be up to 15 percent larger in diameter than the Milky Way, according to ESO.

understand.summary: This image was made with the FORS2 instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope, using blue, visual and red filters plus H-alpha for glowing hydrogen. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The galaxy is far too faint to see in this detail by eye, and the telescope's exposures gather far more light than an eye can.

alt: An edge-on galaxy seen as a band of light with twists in its structure.
